items.definition: a musical instrument with wooden bars you strike with small mallets
items.sentence: In music class Ivy played a cheerful tune on the xylophone.
items.hint: It begins with an x that sounds like z, and phone means sound.

items.definition: a cone-shaped tool that makes your voice much louder
items.sentence: The coach used a megaphone so every swimmer could hear her clearly.
items.hint: Mega means big and phone means sound, so join mega and phone.

items.definition: a curved brass-and-reed instrument often played in jazz bands
items.sentence: Uncle Theo played a smooth saxophone solo at the school fete.
items.hint: Phone means sound; start with saxo and finish with p-h-o-n-e.

items.definition: a word that sounds the same as another but has a different spelling
items.sentence: Our teacher showed us a tricky homophone pair, like bored and board.
items.hint: Homo means same and phone means sound, so join the two roots.

items.definition: the listening tool a doctor uses to hear your heartbeat
items.sentence: The vet used a stethoscope to check the joey's strong heartbeat.
items.hint: Start with stetho, then add scope: s-c-o-p-e.

items.definition: to take one number away from another
items.sentence: First we subtract the smaller number and then check our answer.
items.hint: Sub means under and tract means pull; do not lose the middle t.

items.definition: a three-legged stand that holds a camera steady
items.sentence: Ali steadied the camera on a tripod for our nature documentary.
items.hint: Tri means three and pod means foot, so join tri and pod.

items.definition: a large space rock that travels around the sun
items.sentence: Scientists tracked a distant asteroid as it drifted past Mars.
items.hint: It starts with aster, from the Greek word for star.

items.definition: to use something again instead of throwing it away
items.sentence: Our class learned to recycle paper, cans and glass bottles properly.
items.hint: Cycl means circle; the s sound in the middle is written with a c.

items.definition: half of a round shape, like a rainbow or a protractor
items.sentence: We sat in a quiet semicircle while the ranger showed us lizards.
items.hint: Semi means half; join semi and circle with no extra letters.

items.definition: a flat shape with five straight sides
items.sentence: Ben drew a neat pentagon and measured each of its sides.
items.hint: Penta means five and gon means angle, so write penta then gon.

items.definition: a flat shape with three or more straight sides
items.sentence: A stop sign is a polygon because it has eight straight sides.
items.hint: Poly means many; the vowel after the l is a y, not an i.

items.definition: a period of ten years
items.sentence: Grandad has coached the surf club for more than a decade.
items.hint: Deca means ten, so start with d-e-c-a.

items.definition: a unit for measuring how much space computer files take up
items.sentence: That photo file is nearly one megabyte, so it sends quickly.
items.hint: Mega means big; end with byte, spelled b-y-t-e.

items.definition: a train that runs along a single raised rail
items.sentence: The theme park monorail glided smoothly above the crowded paths.
items.hint: Mono means one; it is simply mono plus rail.

items.definition: to pull something towards you or make it come closer
items.sentence: Bright flowers attract busy bees to our vegetable garden every spring.
items.hint: The prefix at joins the root tract, so double t comes early.

items.definition: to completely change how something looks or works
items.sentence: A little paint can transform an old bike into something amazing.
items.hint: Trans means across and form means shape; join them without changing letters.

items.definition: the matching set of clothes worn by a school or team
items.sentence: Every player wore a clean uniform for the grand final photo.
items.hint: Uni means one; one form means everyone dresses the same way.

items.definition: amazing to look at
items.sentence: The fireworks were so spectacular that the whole beach cheered loudly.
items.hint: Spect means look; after spect comes -acular.

items.definition: to teach someone or tell them how to do something
items.sentence: The lifesavers will instruct us on reading the flags safely.
items.hint: Struct means build, so the word finishes with -struct.

items.definition: a book or piece of writing before it is printed
items.sentence: The author showed us her messy manuscript full of pencil notes.
items.hint: Manu means hand and script means written, so join manu and script.

items.definition: a boat that can travel deep under the water
items.sentence: The model submarine dived slowly to the bottom of the pool.
items.hint: Sub means under and marine means sea; keep the final e.

items.definition: an area of land that belongs to a group or animal
items.sentence: Magpies guard their territory carefully during the nesting season each year.
items.hint: Terra means land; remember the double r and the -ory ending.

items.definition: a short performance to try out for a part or team
items.sentence: Milo practised his lines before the audition for the school play.
items.hint: Audi means hear; start with a-u-d-i, then add -tion.

items.definition: the image you see when light bounces off a shiny surface
items.sentence: She smiled at her reflection in the still water of the creek.
items.hint: Flect means bend; light bends back, and the ending is -tion.

items.definition: to learn something so well you can say it without looking
items.sentence: Tonight I will memorise my speech for assembly on Friday.
items.hint: Australian spelling uses -ise at the end, never -ize.

items.definition: to watch over people to keep things safe and fair
items.sentence: Two teachers supervise the pool gates during every lunch swim.
items.hint: Super means over and vis means see; Australians end it with -ise.

items.definition: a discussion where people strongly disagree
items.sentence: They settled the argument by checking the cricket rule book together.
items.hint: Drop the e from argue before adding -ment.

items.definition: by mistake, without meaning to
items.sentence: Ella accidentally packed two left sneakers for the athletics carnival.
items.hint: Take accidental and add -ly, keeping the full -ally ending.

items.definition: totally, in every way
items.sentence: By lunchtime the rising tide had completely covered the rock pools.
items.hint: Keep the silent e in complete before adding -ly.

items.definition: extremely good
items.sentence: Her science project on native bees received an excellent mark.
items.hint: After exc comes -ellent, with double l and -ent.

items.definition: the steady force of something pushing against a surface
items.sentence: Check the tyre pressure before we ride to the lookout.
items.hint: Start with press and add -ure, keeping the double s.

items.definition: luckily; by good luck
items.sentence: It poured all morning, but fortunately the carnival was moved indoors.
items.hint: Build it from fortunate and simply add -ly.

items.definition: feeling thankful for something kind
items.sentence: We were grateful when the neighbours helped us find our puppy.
items.hint: It comes from the Latin gratus, so start with grate-, not great-.

items.definition: able to do things on your own without help
items.sentence: Camp taught us to be independent by cooking our own dinner.
items.hint: The ending is -ent, and there is no letter a anywhere in it.

items.definition: the words and grammar people use to communicate
items.sentence: Learning a second language helps you understand other cultures better.
items.hint: Remember the u after the g: lang-u-age.

items.definition: the study of numbers, shapes and patterns
items.sentence: Our favourite part of mathematics this term is solving puzzle problems.
items.hint: Say math-e-mat-ics slowly so you do not miss the first e.

items.definition: how strong someone or something is
items.sentence: Rock climbing builds strength in your arms, legs and fingers.
items.hint: Keep the g before the th: streng-th.

items.definition: to manage to do what you set out to do
items.sentence: Keep practising your serves and you will succeed at trials.
items.hint: Double c and then double e: suc-ceed.

items.definition: the one that comes right after the eighth
items.sentence: On his ninth attempt Marcus finally juggled three tennis balls.
items.hint: Drop the e from nine before adding -th.

items.definition: the hard case a caterpillar rests inside while it changes
items.sentence: A pale green chrysalis hung beneath a gum leaf all week.
items.hint: The ch says k and the vowel after chr is a y.

items.definition: an animal that carries its young in a pouch
items.sentence: The wombat is a sturdy marsupial that digs impressive burrows.
items.hint: Say mar-su-pi-al and keep the i before the final al.

items.definition: a small smiling wallaby found on an island near Perth
items.sentence: The famous quokka hopped right past our ranger on the trail.
items.hint: Double k in the middle: quo-kka.

items.definition: a curved throwing stick that can circle back to the thrower
items.sentence: Uncle showed us how a returning boomerang curves through the air.
items.hint: Double o after the b: boom-er-ang.

items.definition: a shy Australian animal with a duck-like bill and webbed feet
items.sentence: We spotted a wild platypus gliding across the shaded mountain stream.
items.hint: Say plat-y-pus; the middle vowel is a y.

items.definition: the planned steps and moves of a dance
items.sentence: Our group invented new choreography for the end-of-year dance concert.
items.hint: The ch says k, and graph means write: chore-o-graphy.

items.definition: a chewy black lolly with a strong sweet flavour
items.sentence: Nonna shared soft liquorice twists with us after the market.
items.hint: Australians spell it liqu-orice, starting like the word liquid.

items.definition: a crisp sweet treat baked from whipped egg whites and sugar
items.sentence: Each crunchy meringue melted away the moment it touched my tongue.
items.hint: It ends with the French -gue, where the ue stays silent: mer-in-gue.

items.definition: a sweet brown spice often sprinkled on doughnuts and porridge
items.sentence: The kitchen smelled of warm cinnamon while the scrolls were baking.
items.hint: Double n in the middle: cin-na-mon.

items.definition: a slow lizard that changes colour to match its background
items.sentence: In the reptile house a chameleon slowly turned leafy green.
items.hint: The ch says k, then a-m-e before leon.

items.definition: grand and very impressive to see
items.sentence: The town hall looked magnificent with fairy lights along its towers.
items.hint: Magni means great; the ending is -ficent, not -ficant.

items.definition: a small mouth organ you play by blowing and breathing in
items.sentence: Jack played a lively harmonica tune around the glowing campfire.
items.hint: It starts like harmony, then ends with -ica.

items.definition: a tall Australian gum tree with strong-smelling leaves
items.sentence: Koalas dozed high in the eucalyptus branches beside our campsite.
items.hint: Start with eu, then remember the y: eu-ca-lyp-tus.

items.definition: music that gradually gets louder and louder
items.sentence: The drums built a huge crescendo before the final chorus began.
items.hint: The sc in the middle says sh in this Italian word: cre-scen-do.

items.definition: a fancy hanging light with many branches of glittering glass
items.sentence: A sparkling chandelier glowed above the dancers at the town ball.
items.hint: The French ending -ier sounds like ear: chand-el-ier.

items.definition: a huge river animal with a wide mouth and short legs
items.sentence: At the wildlife park a hippopotamus yawned right at our group.
items.hint: Say each chunk: hip-po-pot-a-mus, with double p early.

items.definition: a sweet loose-skinned fruit like a small orange
items.sentence: Mum packed a juicy tangerine for my recess snack today.
items.hint: Soft g in the middle and -ine at the end: tan-ge-rine.

items.definition: a person who has more than a million dollars
items.sentence: In the board game Priya became a millionaire by trading wisely.
items.hint: Double l then one n, and finish with -aire.

items.definition: a tube of mirrors and beads that makes changing colourful patterns
items.sentence: Twisting the kaleidoscope made the beads tumble into new star shapes.
items.hint: The tricky part is kalei: k-a-l-e-i, then doscope.

items.definition: a thick creamy sauce people spread inside rolls and salads
items.sentence: Dad stirred homemade mayonnaise through the potato salad for the barbecue.
items.hint: Double n then -aise: may-on-naise.

items.definition: a complete change of body form, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly
items.sentence: We watched the tadpole's metamorphosis into a tiny green frog.
items.hint: Morph means shape; spell the f sound with ph.

items.definition: a warm breakfast made by cooking oats in milk or water
items.sentence: On frosty mornings nothing beats creamy porridge with sliced banana.
items.hint: Double r in the middle and -idge at the end.

items.definition: a small soft red fruit that grows on a prickly bush
items.sentence: Grandpa spread raspberry jam thickly on our warm scones.
items.hint: There is a silent p hiding in the middle: rasp-berry.

items.definition: a large cloth canopy that slows a fall from the sky
items.sentence: In gym class our rainbow parachute billowed above the laughing students.
items.hint: The sh sound is written ch, French style: para-chute.

items.definition: a high swinging bar that circus performers fly between
items.sentence: The acrobat swung from her trapeze high above the safety net.
items.hint: One p and a final silent e: tra-peze.

items.definition: a light dessert with a crisp shell, soft middle and fruit on top
items.sentence: Aunty crowned the pavlova with passionfruit, kiwifruit and whipped cream.
items.hint: Say pav-lo-va; the middle vowel is o, not a.

items.definition: a tree that bursts into purple flowers in late spring
items.sentence: Purple jacaranda petals drifted across the schoolyard in November.
items.hint: Say ja-ca-ran-da; every vowel is an a.

items.definition: a maze of twisting paths that is tricky to escape
items.sentence: The hedge labyrinth at the gardens took us ages to solve.
items.hint: Remember the y after lab: lab-y-rinth.

items.definition: a still waterhole left behind when a river changes course
items.sentence: Dragonflies skimmed across the billabong while we unpacked our lunch.
items.hint: Double l early and one g at the end: billa-bong.

items.definition: a round creamy Australian nut with a very hard shell
items.sentence: We cracked one stubborn macadamia with the special nut tool.
items.hint: Say mac-a-da-mi-a; every vowel is an a except the i.

items.definition: a piece of art carved or shaped from stone, wood or clay
items.sentence: Her sand sculpture of a whale won the beach art prize.
items.hint: Start with sculpt and end with -ure: sculp-ture.

items.definition: when two halves match perfectly, like mirror images
items.sentence: Butterfly wings show perfect symmetry when they open in the sun.
items.hint: Start sym with a y, then double m: sym-me-try.

items.definition: to sing or play notes that blend sweetly together
items.sentence: The choir learned to harmonise before the spring concert.
items.hint: Australian spelling ends with -ise, never -ize.

items.definition: a small hand drum with jingling metal discs around its rim
items.sentence: Zoe shook her tambourine in time with the campfire songs.
items.hint: Remember the sneaky our in the middle: tamb-our-ine.

items.definition: a precious deep-blue gemstone
items.sentence: The museum displayed a glowing sapphire the size of a grape.
items.hint: Double p before the h: sap-phire.

items.definition: feeling delighted because you have won or succeeded
items.sentence: The relay team raised triumphant arms as they crossed the line.
items.hint: Build it from triumph and add -ant, keeping the ph.

items.definition: a bright blue-green colour, like shallow tropical water
items.sentence: The lagoon glowed turquoise under the clear summer sky.
items.hint: After tur comes quoise: q-u-o-i-s-e.

items.definition: a plant with sour red stalks often stewed into desserts
items.sentence: Nanna stewed sweet rhubarb to spoon over our warm custard.
items.hint: A silent h follows the first r: rh-u-barb.

items.definition: a thick creamy dairy food often eaten with fruit
items.sentence: For breakfast Sam layered yoghurt with berries and crunchy oats.
items.hint: Australian spelling keeps the h: yog-h-urt.

items.definition: a long green vegetable often sliced into stir-fries
items.sentence: We picked a giant zucchini from the school garden this morning.
items.hint: Double c then single n: zuc-chi-ni.
